content.title: 'Violent' Price Spike Rocks Gas Traders Who Made Bad Winter Bets
content.summary: Futures prices for natural gas — fuel for home furnaces and power plants alike — jumped 70% in the US over a wild week of trading, as forecasts for deep cold grew steadily worse.  The previous week, prices rose 30% in Europe, where a cold snap combined with geopolitical jitters to drive up the market.  Temperatures in gas-producing parts of the US could drop low enough in coming days to freeze pipelines — potentially choking off supplies just as demand for the fuel soars.
